A missing value in this data usually means the protein was too faint to detect, not that it was
absent at random. limpa turns that into a model: one detection probability curve for the whole
experiment, then a value and a standard error for every protein in every run. Observed values keep
a small standard error; values the curve had to estimate get a wide one, so later fits weight them
less. Nothing is filled in as if it had been measured.

This step writes three objects. `proteins.rds` holds limpa's fit for the protein-level models,
which carry blood as a covariate. `DAList_limpa.rds` holds the complete matrix. `DAList_corrected.rds`
holds the same matrix with each protein's blood slope removed, for methods that cannot carry a
covariate.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(limma)
library(limpa)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
```

## Input

The input is the normalised `DAList`: log2 abundance with `NA` where a protein went undetected.
`blood_rel`, the run's haemoglobin signal relative to its median intensity, comes from
`01_Protein_Filtering`. Centring it (`blood`) makes the model intercepts refer to a run of average
blood content.

```{r}
#| label: input
stage <- here("01_Processing", "03_Quantification")
out <- file.path(stage, "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(normalized = "01_Processing/02_Normalisation/c_data/DAList_normalized.rds")
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
dal <- readRDS(paths[["normalized"]])
values <- as.matrix(dal$data)
stopifnot(identical(dal$metadata$sample_id, colnames(values)))

group_levels <- c("HR_T1", "HR_T2", "HR_T3", "LR_T1", "LR_T2", "LR_T3")
meta <- as_tibble(dal$metadata) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, group_levels), blood = blood_rel - mean(blood_rel))
dim(values)
c(pct_missing = round(100 * mean(is.na(values)), 1))
head(select(meta, sample_id, subject, group, blood_rel, blood))
```

## Detection probability curve

`dpc()` fits the chance that a value is detected as a logistic function of its log2 intensity: the
intercept sets where detection starts, the slope how fast it rises. A slope near 0 would mean
values go missing at random; a steep slope means faint proteins go missing first.

Evidence for this route (decisions log, 2026-10-01): missingness here tracks intensity (Spearman
rho -0.77), and the earlier pipeline's imputation (missForest) filled mid-range values and shrank
the variance. 17 of 49 earlier interaction hits rested on a group cell with 3 or fewer observed
values.

```{r}
#| label: dpc
curve <- dpc(values)
curve$dpc
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dpc
#| fig-cap: "Detection probability against log2 intensity. The curve is limpa's fit."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5
plotDPC(curve)
```

## A value and a standard error for every protein

The input is already summarised to proteins, so each row is its own feature. `dpcQuantByRow()` is
the route the limpa vignette gives for protein-level input, and Gordon Smyth confirmed on the
Bioconductor support site (support.bioconductor.org/p/9163224) that it needs intensity-based log
values, which this matrix is.

```{r}
#| label: quantify
proteins <- dpcQuantByRow(values, dpc = curve, verbose = FALSE)
observed <- proteins$other$n.observations > 0
stopifnot(!anyNA(proteins$E), identical(observed, !is.na(values)))
standard_error <- proteins$other$standard.error
```

One protein with gaps, before and after. Observed runs keep their value and a small standard
error; the missing runs get an estimate from the curve and a wide standard error.

```{r}
#| label: before-after
example <- which(rowSums(!observed) >= 3)[1]
tibble(
  sample_id = colnames(values)[1:8],
  observed = round(values[example, 1:8], 2),
  limpa = round(proteins$E[example, 1:8], 2),
  standard_error = round(standard_error[example, 1:8], 2)
) |>
  print(n = 8)
c(protein = dal$annotation$gene[example], runs_missing = sum(!observed[example, ]))
```

## Blood-corrected matrix

Some methods (gene-set scores, co-expression modules, clustering) take no covariate. For them, each
protein's slope on the blood index is removed with `limma::removeBatchEffect()`. The slope is fitted
beside time point only, `~ 0 + timepoint`, so no HR or LR label shapes the matrix every later
analysis reads. Models that can carry blood as a covariate use `proteins.rds` instead (decisions
log, 2026-10-01).

```{r}
#| label: blood-correct
corrected <- remove_blood_effect(proteins$E, meta$blood, model.matrix(~ 0 + timepoint, meta))
```

Each protein's Spearman correlation with the blood index, before and after removal, split by how
many of the 45 runs measured the protein.

```{r}
#| label: blood-check
blood_rho <- \(m) as.vector(cor(t(m), meta$blood, method = "spearman"))
tibble(
  runs_measured = cut(rowSums(observed), c(0, 10, 20, 39, 45)),
  before = abs(blood_rho(proteins$E)), after = abs(blood_rho(corrected))
) |>
  group_by(runs_measured) |>
  summarise(proteins = n(), median_rho_before = median(before), median_rho_after = median(after))
```

Removal works for well-measured proteins and fails for sparse ones: it raises their correlation
with blood. The likely cause is that `removeBatchEffect()` fits one slope across measured and
curve-estimated values, then subtracts slope × blood from both, stamping blood onto estimates that
never carried it. This is an open methodological problem, not yet fixed. Every analysis that reads
`DAList_corrected.rds` inherits it for proteins measured in few runs.

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  identical(dim(proteins$E), dim(values)),
  identical(dim(corrected), dim(values)),
  !anyNA(corrected),
  all(standard_error > 0),
  identical(meta$sample_id, colnames(corrected))
)
se_observed <- median(standard_error[observed])
se_missing <- median(standard_error[!observed])
c(median_se_observed = se_observed, median_se_missing = se_missing)
```

## Summary

`r round(100 * mean(!observed), 1)`% of values are missing. The detection curve has intercept
`r round(curve$dpc[1], 2)` and slope `r round(curve$dpc[2], 2)` on the logit scale.
`r nrow(values)` proteins now have a value in all `r ncol(values)` runs;
`r sum(rowSums(observed) == ncol(values))` were measured in every run, and the median protein in
`r median(rowSums(observed))`. A missing value's median standard error is
`r round(se_missing / se_observed, 1)` times an observed one's.

## Save

`proteins.rds` feeds the protein-level contrasts. `DAList_limpa.rds` and `DAList_corrected.rds`
feed the set, module, classification and trait steps. `Figures/S01_QC` reads the workbook. The
`sample_correlation` sheet centres each protein on its mean first, so the correlation reflects how
runs differ rather than the abundance order every run shares.

```{r}
#| label: save
as_dalist <- function(data) {
  list(data = data, annotation = dal$annotation, metadata = meta, observed = observed)
}
saveRDS(
  list(proteins = proteins, metadata = meta, annotation = dal$annotation),
  file.path(out, "proteins.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
saveRDS(as_dalist(proteins$E), file.path(out, "DAList_limpa.rds"), compress = "xz")
saveRDS(as_dalist(corrected), file.path(out, "DAList_corrected.rds"), compress = "xz")

write_workbook(
  list(
    curve = tibble(
      term = names(curve$dpc), estimate = unname(curve$dpc),
      pct_missing = 100 * mean(!observed)
    ),
    proteins = tibble(
      uniprot_id = rownames(values), gene = dal$annotation$gene,
      n_observed = rowSums(observed), prop_observed = rowMeans(observed),
      mean_observed = rowMeans(values, na.rm = TRUE), mean_complete = rowMeans(proteins$E),
      median_se_observed = apply(ifelse(observed, standard_error, NA), 1, median, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_se_missing = apply(ifelse(observed, NA, standard_error), 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    blood = select(meta, sample_id, subject, group, blood_rel, blood),
    sample_correlation = as_tibble(cor(corrected - rowMeans(corrected)), rownames = "sample_id")
  ),
  c(
    "DPC intercept and slope on the logit scale, and the share of values missing.",
    paste(
      "Per protein: values observed, mean log2 abundance where observed and over the complete",
      "matrix, and the median standard error where observed and where missing."
    ),
    "Per sample: blood index (HBB and HBA1 against the sample median) and its centred value.",
    "Pearson correlation between samples, each protein centred, on the blood-corrected matrix."
  ),
  file.path(out, "quantification.xlsx"),
  inputs, paths
)
```
